findings.title: APP_DEBUG is enabled
findings.description: APP_DEBUG is set to true. In production, this exposes detailed error messages including stack traces, database queries, and environment variables to end users.
findings.remediation: Set APP_DEBUG=false in your production .env file. Use Laravel's logging system for error tracking instead.

findings.title: APP_ENV is set to 'local'
findings.description: The application environment suggests a non-production configuration. If this is a production server, this may cause debug features to be enabled and performance optimizations to be skipped.
findings.remediation: Set APP_ENV=production on production servers.

findings.title: Database password is empty
findings.description: DB_PASSWORD is set to an empty string. While this may be valid for local development with trust authentication, it's a security risk if this configuration reaches production.
findings.remediation: Set a strong database password for non-local environments.

findings.title: CORS allows all origins
findings.description: config/cors.php allows requests from any origin ('*'). This permits cross-site data theft if authenticated endpoints return sensitive data.
findings.remediation: Specify allowed origins: 'allowed_origins' => [env('FRONTEND_URL')],

findings.title: CORS allows credentials with wildcard origin
findings.description: CORS is configured with both 'supports_credentials' => true and wildcard allowed_origins. This combination allows any website to make authenticated requests to your API.
findings.remediation: Never combine 'supports_credentials' => true with wildcard origins. Specify exact allowed origins.

findings.title: [CVE-2026-30838] league/commonmark@2.8.0 — CommonMark has DisallowedRawHtml extension bypass via whitespace in HTML tag names
findings.description: CommonMark has DisallowedRawHtml extension bypass via whitespace in HTML tag names
findings.remediation:
Upgrade league/commonmark to 2.8.1 or later:
  composer require league/commonmark:2.8.1

findings.title: [CVE-2025-54370] phpoffice/phpspreadsheet@4.5.0 — PhpSpreadsheet vulnerable to SSRF when reading and displaying a processed HTML document in the browser
findings.description: PhpSpreadsheet vulnerable to SSRF when reading and displaying a processed HTML document in the browser
findings.remediation:
Upgrade phpoffice/phpspreadsheet to 1.30.0 or later:
  composer require phpoffice/phpspreadsheet:1.30.0

findings.title: Weak random number generation

  random_int($min, $max)         // secure integer
  Str::random(40)                // secure string (Laravel)
  random_bytes(32)               // secure raw bytes

findings.title: DB::raw() with variable interpolation
findings.description: DB::raw() is called with a PHP variable, which may lead to SQL injection if the variable contains unsanitized user input. Laravel's query builder automatically escapes parameters — use bindings instead of raw SQL.
findings.remediation:
Use parameter bindings:
  DB::raw('COUNT(*) as count')           // safe — no variables
  DB::select('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?', [$id])  // safe — bound
Avoid:
  DB::raw("WHERE name = '$name'")        // vulnerable

findings.title: Shell command execution function
findings.description: PHP shell execution functions (exec, system, shell_exec, passthru, popen, proc_open) are being used. If any argument includes user input, this leads to OS command injection.
findings.code_snippet: Log::warning('Queue health check skipped because exec() is unavailable.');
findings.remediation:
Avoid shell commands when possible. If necessary:
  - Use escapeshellarg() and escapeshellcmd() for all arguments
  - Use Symfony\Component\Process\Process for safer execution
  - Validate and whitelist expected input values
